question: When GA spreads an IX-supplied 3D voicing cloud, which visual comparisons remain justified, and what does the pinned renderer actually validate?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
hypothesis: Tracing a fixed three-point payload through the pinned renderer will show that positive spread can reveal overlap while changing apparent pairwise distance, and that the loader's shallow validation cannot establish complete instrument-block coverage.
evidence: At GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924, ReactComponents/ga-react-components/src/components/PrimeRadiant/VoicingCloud.ts checks binary float count against meta.total * 3, copies instrument blocks into a sequential destination, uses per-instrument RGB, and adds (Math.random() + Math.random() - 1) * spread separately to each coordinate when spread is positive.

The pinned setSpread rebuilds from retained basePositions, so zero restores coordinates and repeated positive calls resample. setPointSize changes PointsMaterial.size without rebuilding positions. Defaults are spread 1.5 and point size 0.3.

The fixed synthetic fixture has three points at x 0, approximately 0.2, and 10; nine floats satisfy the length check. Hypothetical x draw pairs (0.1, 0.1) and (0.9, 0.9) at spread 1.5 move the first two displayed x coordinates to -1.2 and approximately 1.4, increasing their apparent gap from approximately 0.2 to 2.6. These are chosen draws, not observed browser output.

A second synthetic fixture keeps total 3 and nine floats but has two one-point instrument blocks. The top-level checks can pass although only two destination slots are copied and the remaining typed-array slot stays zero. The source does not validate block coverage, finite values, or the meaning of 3D distance relative to the full OPTIC-K embedding.

ReactComponents/ga-react-components/src/components/PrimeRadiant/ForceRadiant.tsx at the same commit loads the cloud when the URL has a voicings parameter and permits a voicings_url override. No IX payload, browser run, usability measurement, subject review, learner attempt, or publication was performed for this research cycle. Duration was not instrumented; duration_seconds=0 records that limit.
